text: EX-99.1 9 altg-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Alta Equipment Group Agrees to Acquire Jackson Group Peterbilt in Proposed Transformative Deal Proposed acquisition expected to create scaled dealership platform for essential equipment that powers the industrial economy Would add commercial truck vertical with premier Peterbilt dealership platform with 34 locations in the western U.S. Expected to enhance earnings quality and cash generation and support continued deleveraging Proposed strategic investment from Viking Global Investors expected to help finance acquisition and support company’s focus on lean operations and capital efficiency Livonia, MI. – November 23, 2026 – Alta Equipment Group Inc. (NYSE: ALTG) ("Alta" or the "Company"), a leading integrated equipment dealership platform in North America, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Jackson Group Peterbilt ("JGP"), a full-service commercial truck dealership group with an expansive footprint in the western United States. Under the terms of the agreement, Alta has agreed to acquire JGP for an estimated enterprise value of approximately $399 million, representing approximately 6.3x LTM Adjusted EBITDA as of September 30, 2026, or approximately 5.7x LTM Adjusted EBITDA after giving effect to approximately $40 million of estimated tax benefits associated with the transaction. The proposed transaction would be financed with a combination of cash and Alta common stock. Upon completion, the acquisition is expected to broaden Alta’s integrated industrial equipment dealership platform to include commercial trucks, material handling and construction equipment with 119 locations across 22 U.S. states and three Canadian provinces. Alta expects the transaction to be accretive to its earnings and cash flow profile in the first 12 months following closing, and, on a pro forma basis, expects net leverage to decline from approximately 4.8x to 3.7x proforma as of September 30, 2026 to an expected 3.6x at year-end 2026. “This is a transformative opportunity for Alta to establish a coast-to-coast dealership platform and broaden our business across equipment categories, end markets and customers,” said Ryan Greenawalt, Chief Executive Officer of Alta. “We expect the addition of JGP’s premier commercial truck dealership platform to create a third scaled segment for Alta, enhance our recurring aftermarket mix, and strengthen our cash generation capacity. Together, we anticipate being positioned well for continued growth and greater resilience across market cycles.” JGP operates 34 dealerships, including 12 full-service locations and 19 parts and service locations, as well as multiple parts-only locations and body shops. The business supports more than 50,000 customers across freight, vocational, construction, waste, municipal and other essential applications. JGP generated approximately $906 million in revenue and $63.3 million in Adjusted EBITDA for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026. In connection with the transaction, Alta has entered into an agreement providing for a $338.4 million strategic investment from entities managed by Viking Global Investors LP (“Viking”) with economic rights that are pari passu with Alta common stock. The investment, which is conditioned on the closing of the acquisition, will help fund the acquisition as well as support Alta’s focus on lean operations and capital efficiency. In connection with the closing of the financing, Matt Vaughan, President of Battelle Memorial Institute, and Jeff Figg, who spent nearly 20 years as an executive at Danaher Corporation, are expected to join Alta’s Board of Directors. The acquisition is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Alta’s stockholders of the issuance of securities in the transactions, receipt of required regulatory and other third-party approvals and satisfaction or waiver, as applicable, of other closing conditions. Proposed Acquisition Expected to Provide Strategic and Financial Benefits • Would Create a Leading Dealership Platform. The proposed combination would bring together proven dealership platforms with a shared focus on delivering essential equipment, product support and uptime to customers. • Would Add a Scaled Commercial Trucks Vertical. JGP’s Peterbilt dealership platform with OEM-protected territories is expected to add a new scaled dealership vertical for additional growth and broaden Alta’s equipment and end-market exposure. • Expected to Support Growth Through Greater Scale and Diversification. On a combined basis giving effect to the acquisition, Alta and JGP generated approximately $2.7 billion in revenue and $226 million in Adjusted EBITDA for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026. The proposed combination is expected to expand Alta’s geographic, equipment category and customer exposure. • Expected to Improve Earnings Quality and Capital Efficiency. The combination is expected to grow Alta’s installed base and enhance its recurring aftermarket mix, increasing the contribution of aftermarket to gross profit to 59% and improving absorption from 77% to 89% on a proforma basis. JGP’s capital-efficient business model is expected to improve Alta’s return on invested capital. • Expected to Strengthen Cash Generation and Support Deleveraging. The combination is expected to enhance cash generation and financial flexibility, supporting continued deleveraging towards the Company’s new leverage target of 2.0x – 3.0x Adjusted EBITDA, while preserving capacity for disciplined organic growth and M&A. Additional Transaction Details • The transaction is expected to provide meaningful tax benefits, including the potential utilization of approximately $170 million in federal net operating losses, subject to applicable limitations and the availability of taxable income. • Affiliates of Viking have agreed to invest $338.4 million in Alta’s new Series B Convertible Preferred Stock. The investment is priced at the 60-day volume-weighted average price of $6.33 per share of Alta common stock on an as-converted basis. The Series B shares will be non-voting and will have economic rights that are pari passu with Alta common stock and, as such, have no liquidation preference, preferred coupon or maturity date. • Upon closing of the financing, Viking will have the right to designate two members of Alta’s board of directors and one non-voting board observer, as well as consent rights over certain significant corporate actions, in each case, subject to minimum ownership thresholds and the terms of the definitive documents. Viking’s aggregate voting power upon conversion of the Series B shares would be capped at 49.9% at all times. • The seller of JGP is expected to become a significant shareholder of Alta, receiving $30 million of deal consideration in common stock at $6.33 per share. About Jackson Group Peterbilt Jackson Group Peterbilt is a leading full-service commercial truck dealership platform with 34 locations across eight western states. JGP sells and supports new and used trucks and provides parts, service, leasing, fleet support and body shop capabilities. The company is a premier Peterbilt partner and has received 20 consecutive PACCAR “Best in Class” awards. JGP serves more than 50,000 customers across freight, vocational, construction, waste, municipal and other essential applications. About Alta Equipment Group Inc. Alta owns and operates one of the largest integrated equipment dealership platforms in North America. Through its branch network, the Company sells, rents and provides parts and service support for a broad portfolio of specialized equipment, including lift trucks and aerial work platforms, cranes, earthmoving equipment and other material handling and construction equipment. Alta has operated as an equipment dealership for 42 years and has 85 locations across 15 states and three Canadian provinces. Alta offers customers a one-stop shop for equipment, parts and service. More information can be found at www.altaequipment.com . About Viking Global Investors Founded in 1999, Viking Global Investors is a global investment firm with a long-term, fundamental, research-intensive approach to investing. Viking manages more than $54 billion of capital across public and private investments (as of September 30, 2026). Viking has offices in Stamford, New York, London, and San Francisco, and is registered as an investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. For more information, please visit www.vikingglobal.com. Financial Information JGP financial information has not been audited by Alta or its auditors and remains subject to finalization. The combined financial information presented in this release is provided for illustrative purposes only and is not necessarily indicative of the results that would have been achieved had the Transactions occurred at the beginning of the periods presented or of future results. *Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement the financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“GAAP”), we disclose non-GAAP financial measure Adjusted EBITDA in this press release because we believe it is a useful performance measures that assist in an effective evaluation of operating performance when compared to our peers, without regard to financing methods or capital structure. We believe such measure is useful for investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management. However, such measure is not a financial measure calculated in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered as a substitute for, or in isolation from, net income (loss), revenues, operating profit, debt, or any other operating performance measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, as adjusted for certain projected non-operating items, and reduced by interest expense associated with new truck floorplan financing. We exclude these items from net income (loss) in arriving at Adjusted EBITDA because these amounts are either non-cash, non-recurring, or can vary substantially within the industry depending upon accounting methods and book values of assets, capital structures, and the method by which the assets were acquired. Certain items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA are significant components in understanding and assessing a company’s financial performance. For example, items such as a company’s cost of capital and tax structure, certain one-time, non-cash or non-recurring items as well as the historic costs of depreciable assets, are not reflected in Adjusted EBITDA. Our presentation of Adjusted EBITDA should not be construed as an indication that results will be unaffected by the items excluded from these metrics. Our computation of Adjusted EBITDA may not be identical to other similarly titled measures of other companies. For a reconciliation of non-GAAP measures to their most comparable measures under GAAP, please see the table entitled “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” at the end of this press release.
